Theme

Computing & programming

device noun

a gadget: a phone, tablet or the like

also devices, gadget, electronic device, mobile device, appliance

classical

Traupman 305: disk drive īnstrūmentum
Caes. BG 6.30: mīlitāre (Lewis & Short)

īnstrūmentum, īnstrūmentī n.

noun, second declension

a device, an instrument

Classically any implement or tool, and as a collective, equipment (see tool). An electronic device is īnstrūmentum ēlectronicum; where the kind is clear, name it: tēlephōnum, computātrum.

Other words

  • māchinula, māchinulae f. — a small machine, a gadget

    noun, first declension · also used · late Latin · Paul. Nol. Carm. 26.458 (Lewis & Short)

    Late (Lewis & Short), but the modern word for small appliances, as in māchinula phōtographica (see camera) and māchinula calculātōria (see calculator).

  • apparātus, apparātūs m. — apparatus, equipment

    noun, fourth declension · also used · classical · Traupman 261: hardware apparātus

    Classically a preparing, then the things prepared: equipment, apparatus (Cic.); for a single device, too wide.

Examples

  • Ante cēnam omnia īnstrūmenta ēlectronica sēpōnite.

    Put all your devices away before dinner.composed

See also telephone, computer, tool, machine, camera, calculator, electronic.

SourcesLewis & Short: instrumentum · Lewis & Short: machinula · Lewis & Short: apparatus

John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, pp. 261, 305.
